submission.justification: Algorithm-L1 with a threshold of 35.5 GeV is the optimal choice. Through systematic simulation testing, this configuration achieves the highest signal efficiency (87.716%) at the allocated 8 kHz rate among all deployable options. Algorithm-L3, while offering higher efficiency (~92.7%), exceeds the Level-1 latency budget (5.8 us vs. 4.0 us limit) and cannot be deployed in the Level-1 trigger hardware. Algorithm-L2 achieves only ~73-74% efficiency across all tested thresholds. Algorithm-L1 meets all hardware constraints with a latency of 3.1 us (well within the 4.0 us budget), fits within FPGA resources, and delivers significantly better performance than Algorithm-L2 while being the best deployable solution available.

requirements.requirement: Achieve the highest possible signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 at 35.5 GeV achieves 87.716% signal efficiency at the 8 kHz allocated rate, which is the highest among all deployable algorithms (Algorithm-L2 achieves only ~73-74%, and Algorithm-L3 is not deployable due to latency constraints).

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be one of the three candidates listed in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 (sliding-window clustering with learned calibration) is one of the three candidates specified in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: The algorithm must be deployable in the Level-1 trigger hardware
requirements.evidence: Algorithm-L1 meets all hardware constraints: latency of 3.1 us is within the 4.0 us budget (firmware_testbench_results.md), fits within FPGA resource budget (candidate_specs.md), and has sufficient optical link bandwidth (links.md).
The recommended threshold of 35.5 GeV falls within the specified range of 20-60 GeV.

requirements.evidence: Submitting single recommendation: Algorithm-L1 with threshold 35.5 GeV.
